## Purpose and entry points
TEAMMATES is a cloud-hosted peer-evaluation and student-feedback system. It is a Java server plus Angular SPA. Server startup is `src/main/java/teammates/main/Application.java`; servlet deployment/static fallback are configured under `src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml`. The browser app bootstraps at `src/web/main.ts`, with application routing in `src/web/app/app.routes.ts`.

## Client application
The Angular client provides separate student, instructor, administrator, maintainer, session-link, and static/public workflows. Role/page route partitions are under `src/web/app/pages-student/student.routes.ts`, `src/web/app/pages-instructor/instructor.routes.ts`, and `src/web/app/pages-admin/admin.routes.ts`. Domain services issue API calls and encapsulate client state/transformations, e.g. `src/web/services/feedback-sessions.service.ts`, `src/web/services/feedback-responses.service.ts`, and `src/web/services/auth.service.ts`. Route guards protect role- and session-key-based access in `src/web/route-guards/role.guard.ts` and `src/web/route-guards/session-key.guard.ts`.

## HTTP API, authentication, and authorization
Requests enter servlet/filter boundaries through `src/main/java/teammates/ui/servlets/WebApiServlet.java`; web pages, OAuth/login/logout, health checks, request tracing, origin validation, and security headers are neighboring servlet components. API dispatch maps endpoints to action classes via `src/main/java/teammates/ui/webapi/ActionFactory.java`. Actions validate request DTOs, authenticate/authorize through action base classes and `GateKeeper`, invoke domain logic, and return output DTOs. Key boundaries are `src/main/java/teammates/ui/request`, `src/main/java/teammates/ui/output`, and `src/main/java/teammates/ui/webapi`.

## Core feedback and course domain
Business rules are organized in logic services: courses/enrollment, feedback sessions/questions/responses, permissions, accounts, notifications, and deadline extensions. Main orchestration resides in `src/main/java/teammates/logic/core/FeedbackSessionsLogic.java`, `src/main/java/teammates/logic/core/FeedbackQuestionsLogic.java`, and `src/main/java/teammates/logic/core/FeedbackResponsesLogic.java`. The feedback model supports polymorphic question and response types through transfer definitions in `src/main/java/teammates/common/datatransfer/questions` and persisted subtype entities in `src/main/java/teammates/storage/entity/questions`. Results flow from stored responses through per-question calculators in `src/main/java/teammates/logic/statistics` into session/result API outputs.

## Persistence and schema evolution
Logic accesses relational persistence only through storage APIs such as `src/main/java/teammates/storage/api/FeedbackSessionsDb.java` and `src/main/java/teammates/storage/api/FeedbackResponsesDb.java`. Hibernate-backed entities define users, course rosters, sessions, questions, responses, permissions, notifications, and magic links under `src/main/java/teammates/storage/entity`. Database schema changes are Liquibase-managed from `src/main/resources/db/changelog/db.changelog-root.xml`; Hibernate lifecycle is initialized by `src/main/java/teammates/ui/servlets/HibernateContextListener.java`.

## Asynchronous and external integrations
Time-driven session reminders and email work are exposed as automated API actions and queued behind the `TaskQueuer` abstraction. Queue implementations include Google Cloud Tasks and local execution: `src/main/java/teammates/logic/external/GoogleCloudTasksService.java` and `src/main/java/teammates/logic/external/LocalTaskQueueService.java`. Email composition/delivery is separated into `src/main/java/teammates/logic/email/EmailQueueService.java` and transport adapters for Mailjet, SendGrid, SMTP, or no-op under `src/main/java/teammates/logic/external/email`. Authentication supports Google OAuth and a development login handler; reCAPTCHA is similarly abstracted with Google and empty implementations.

## Deployment and runtime boundaries
The backend is Java/Gradle and packaged for servlet/container deployment; the frontend is TypeScript/Angular built via `angular.json`. Deployment artifacts cover Google App Engine (`src/main/appengine/app.template.yaml`, `src/main/appengine/queue.yaml`) and Docker (`src/main/docker/Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`). App Engine is therefore the principal cloud integration, with Cloud Tasks used for background work; production identity, database, mail, and CAPTCHA behavior are environment-configured.
